line.comment: * CI = Coordinated Invasion.
* Chooses the leading Battlegroup (champion), then the sector target. Then fills up with other member Battlegroups at similar jump distance like the champion. Then starts the operation.
* returns FALSE if the chosen operation type is currently not possible. Returns the target sector if a CI could be started.
* Phanon doesnt have access to certain types of CIs
* minimum power rating of individual Battlegroups
* minimum power rating for the entire operation. The default 2000 points equal a combat strength of 4x M2 destroyers
* CI type
* Hector: This means that when they want to use that CI against the player they measure the jump distance from the player sector they want to invade towards all their own
* sectors and the average cannot be greater than 13 jumps. This setting doesn't need to be so high. It was just a gut feeling at the time. Everything was balanced with the
* medium map size in mind.
* Mordan 5 - Adjusted from 13 to 10 so that they need to be a bit closer to you before sending major fleets after you.
* Expanded 2.2: Temporary; will be reworked in later version.
* FoF overhauled the war system and did a great job with it.

line.comment: * our target sector is often the one closest to the champion
* some types of CIs are very picky. This greatly reduces our sector target selection and we never want weak factions to send their fleets too far away
* even if we can only target sectors in general proximity to the rest of our empire we can send our fleets a bit further than that
* for the more aggressive types of CIs we actually want longer range to be more likely

line.comment: * now begin to fill up with other Battlegroups which are at same jump distance as our champion so that nobody arrives at his standby position at vastly different times
* ^^^ this is the max 'width' of the 'search band' (in sectors on the galaxy map). The baseline is the distance of the Champion member BattleGroup
* can also be descriibed as: how much closer OR further away than the champion can the other members be. Goal here is to not have anyone waiting for long.
* we can repeat this and expand our 'search band' up to a top width of 6 sectors. It starts at the same jump distance to the target sector as our Champion
* only add a member if it is inside the search band, aka 'roughly the same jump distance as our champion'. Not too close, not too far away.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: No duplicates!
* Do not exceed the maximum CI power.
* Champion alone may exceed the cap; do not add further Battlegroups.
* once we have at least our minimum power we randomly stop to add more squadrons
* the more defensive CIs are much more likely to fill up further
* always likely to use extra power against the player
* after we added all BGs which are at same jump distance as the champion we start expanding our search band around the target sector to fill the CI with more BGs
* got enough power now?

* Add-Ons 2.0.2 (comments only): CIs do not use jump holes, only permanent gates.
* target sector
* member array, including the CI leader
* potential rally jumpgates must lead straight into the target sector
* each member BG gets its closest possible rally jumpgate and the sector saved as local variable (these also get handed over should a leader switch happen)
* an active rallyGate variable blocks retreat checks (Mayhem.Squadron.AssessRetreat) and changes general fleet behavior (Mayhem.Task.Squadron.BattleGroup)
* we stop any retreating
* restart each member squadron
* if player gets targeted everyone pities him and allows to sign truces again
* Add-Ons 1.4: Not for OCV players.
* Add-Ons 2.2: Standardized infamy.
